sections.html:
Charles County is in Southern Maryland. La Plata is the county seat, and Waldorf is the biggest community, with 81,410 residents in 2020. The county counted 166,617 people that year and an estimated 176,593 by 2025, a rise of 6.0 percent.

Waldorf works as a bedroom community for Washington, D.C., with MTA commuter bus routes 901, 903, 905 and 907 running between the two. The Indian Head naval installation on the Potomac is the largest single employer. Federal and base-related jobs can move a household on a fixed schedule, so some owners here want a closing date that will not slip.

Roughly 29 percent of the county's total area is water, so creeks, swamps and shoreline appear in many property descriptions.

Most Charles County sellers fall into one of four settings, and each has its own buyers and its own tax picture.

  • Waldorf: a large planned community on U.S. Route 301, where Maryland Route 5 begins.
  • La Plata: the county seat, a town with its own municipal rate.
  • Indian Head: a town tied to the naval base, also with its own municipal rate.
  • Rural Charles: Nanjemoy, Port Tobacco Village, Newburg, Bryantown and similar places, where lots are bigger, wells and septic systems are common, and water is never far off.

Towns charge a separate rate, so the same price can produce a very different bill depending on which side of a town line the house sits.

Real property tax here is billed and collected by the Treasurer. July is when full-year bills go out. Live in the house as your principal residence and you can pay in two parts: the first installment by September 30, and the second, plus a service charge, by December 31.

New construction and improvements generate supplemental bills, generally mailed in October (three-quarter year), January (half year) and April (quarter year). If your lender pays the tax from escrow, give it your bill and read the escrow analysis to confirm the payment was made.

  • Office: 200 Baltimore Street, La Plata, MD 20646. Mail goes to P.O. Box 2607.
  • Phone: 301-645-0685
  • Hours: weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Waldorf payment center closes from 11:15 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. each day.
  • Assessment questions: SDAT sets values and answers at 301-932-2440.

Call the Treasurer for the current interest rate and service charge amount before you pay a late or split bill.

A house in unincorporated Charles County carried a combined real property rate of 1.2050 per $100 of value in the fiscal 2025 state figures, and towns stack their own rate over that.

The special rate of 0.0640 applies in the unincorporated area and in the towns listed. Port Tobacco totals 1.2450. You can test a bill with a calculator: take the taxable assessment, divide by 100, then multiply by the total rate.

Transfer and recordation tax

Maryland's local tax tables show Charles County with a 0.5 percent transfer tax and a recordation figure of $5.00 for fiscal 2025, rising to $7.00 for fiscal 2026. The final charges are printed on the settlement statement the title company prepares.

Charles County offers several credits, and SDAT reviews the applications. The list covers the Homestead Tax Credit, the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit (based on income), a senior tax credit and an exemption for 100 percent disabled former service members. Credits also exist for a perpetual conservation easement, for the surviving spouse of a fallen EMS officer and for volunteer emergency responders.

How to appeal your assessment

If the value looks too high, the state process applies here as it does everywhere in Maryland.

  1. First level: the Supervisor of Assessments, which must hear from you within 45 days of the date on the notice. The control number printed on the notice lets you file online, or you can mail a paper form.
  2. Second level: the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board. You have 30 days from the Supervisor's final notice, and nothing is charged.
  3. Last level: the Maryland Tax Court, 30 days after the board rules. The hearing is held in person and the case is heard from scratch.

New owners get their own window. If the house changed hands from January 1 through June 30, the buyer has 60 days from the transfer date to appeal, provided the deed is recorded.

Charles County tries to keep its floodplain open so water can spread and drain downstream. A house inside a mapped Special Flood Hazard Area is treated differently from one outside it. Homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage, and owners can buy a National Flood Insurance Program policy through an insurance agent.

If your house sits near the Potomac, a creek or a swamp, expect the buyer's lender to ask about its flood zone. Look up your parcel on the FEMA map before listing, and keep any flood insurance paperwork where you can find it. A flood designation can pull offers down.

When property tax is not paid, Maryland lets the county auction the debt as a lien. You still own the house, but whoever wins the auction can collect and, in time, ask a court to foreclose. Charles County holds its sale in May.

  • A notice goes out at least 30 days before the first advertisement, and the advertisement repeats weekly for four weeks.
  • Redemption stays open until a court ends it for good. Each month of delay adds cost.
  • A foreclosure filing can come six months after the sale, or nine for an owner-occupied home. If nothing is filed in two years, the certificate is void.

A house that sells before the auction usually has the tax paid by the title company from the proceeds. For help, the State Tax Sale Ombudsman answers at 410-767-4994, and its Homeowner Protection Program assists limited-income, elderly and disabled owners.

sections.h2: Clearing a tax balance at closing
sections.html:
A house with tax behind can still be sold. Get the Treasurer to quote what is owed through your planned closing date, give that quote to the title company, and the balance is deducted from what you receive. Aim to finish before the May sale if you can, because once a lien is auctioned the payoff grows with added costs.

Selling for cash avoids a buyer lender's appraisal and repair requests, which helps if the house needs work while interest piles up. Whichever route you take, bring the latest bill, any escrow statement from your lender and your photo ID to the first conversation with the title company.

faqs.q: When is Charles County property tax due?
faqs.a: Full-year bills are mailed in July. Principal residence owners can pay in two parts, September 30 and December 31, with a service charge on the second. Call the Treasurer for the current interest rate.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Charles County tax bill?
faqs.a: Dial 301-645-0685, or stop by 200 Baltimore Street in La Plata on a weekday. For the assessed value itself, call SDAT at 301-932-2440.

faqs.q: Why is La Plata taxed higher than the open county?
faqs.a: In the fiscal 2025 table, La Plata totals 1.4130 per $100 and the unincorporated area totals 1.2050. Indian Head totals 1.5060. The town adds its own rate, and figures reset yearly.

faqs.q: Can I sell with back tax owed?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays the tax from your proceeds, whether that happens before the auction or while the lien can still be redeemed. Get a payoff figure with a closing date attached, because interest and fees keep changing it.

faqs.q: How often is the tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, in May. A property is sold only if the account is still unpaid when the sale comes around.
